transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. ...Well, my wife thought I should come in. It's just... some things going on at work. 

I'm working on this environmental modeling contract, and... well, I'm pretty sure the people on it have been tracking my revisions. They're planting errors in the datasets. Just to make it look like I can't lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just... you know, version-control mistakes. But... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you been hearing any voices or sounds that other people around you do not seem to hear?
No... I haven't noticed anything like that. Just... just the issues with the datasets.
Aside from your concerns about the data, have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to focus, organize your daily routine, or feel motivated to engage in your usual activities?

I don't know. Maybe. ...I guess I just sit around more. Mostly at my desk. Or out in the garage... I can just sit out there for hours. My telescope is just... sitting there covered up. 

I know I used to like doing things. Going to astronomy nights, or... hiking. Even mentoring the younger analysts at work. But... I don't know. I just don't feel much pull to start anything lately. Or to talk to anyone.
Have you experienced any recent changes in your memory, confusion, or physical health that you or your doctor have been concerned about?
No. I don't think so. My memory is fine, I guess. And I'm not confused. Physically... I feel fine. Just... nothing like that.
Have these concerns about your work and the datasets been present even during times when you have felt more like your usual self, or do they only seem to happen when you are feeling this low?

I don't... I'm not really sure. I haven't kept track of it like that. 

The issues with the data are just... they're always there. I don't really know about feeling low or... whatever. It's just how things are right now.
Have you ever gone through periods where your mood was so low that you could barely get out of bed, or periods where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or impulsive?
No. I don't... I don't get like that. I get out of bed. I just... sit at my desk, like I said. I'm not... bouncing off the walls or anything. Just normal.
Over the past six months or longer, have you consistently felt like you have less energy to talk to people, or have you found it difficult to express your thoughts or feelings clearly?

I guess I just... don't talk as much. It's not that I can't express things, I just don't really have the drive to. 

I used to do a lot. Hiking... I used to mentor some of the younger analysts at work. Went to astronomy nights. Now I just... sit. Sometimes at my desk, sometimes out in the garage. The telescope is out there, still covered up. I can sit there for hours. I just don't feel the pull to start anything anymore. Or talk to anyone about it.
Looking back, have you felt this lack of drive to talk to people or engage in your hobbies for at least the past six months?
I suppose so. Yeah, probably about that long. It's just been a while since I've really wanted to do much of anything.
When you are at work or talking to your wife, have you been told that your speech is difficult to follow, or that you seem to be acting in a way that is disorganized or hard for others to understand?
No... I don't think so. My wife hasn't said anything about that. And at work, when I do need to say something, they understand me fine. I'm not... disorganized. I just don't talk much.
When you are interacting with your wife or colleagues, have they mentioned that your facial expressions seem limited or that you seem less emotionally responsive than you used to be?

My wife... she might have mentioned something like that. That I just look blank, or that I'm hard to read lately. I don't really know. 

Like I said before, I mostly just sit at my desk or out in the garage for hours. I know I used to do all those things... the hiking, the astronomy nights. But I just don't feel much pull to do anything, or talk to anyone. So I guess... I guess there's just not much for me to react to anymore.

Aside from your concerns about the datasets, have you ever felt that you have unusual or special perceptions, such as believing that random events or ordinary objects have a specific, hidden meaning intended only for you?
No... I don't think so. I'm not sure what you mean, really. Things are just... things. I haven't noticed any hidden meanings or anything like that. Just what I already told you about the data.
Have you noticed any changes in your personal hygiene, such as struggling to keep up with showering, changing clothes, or taking care of yourself, over these past several months?
No... I don't think so. I still shower and everything. Just my normal routine. I haven't had any trouble taking care of myself.
Have you ever found yourself doing things that seem strange or out of place to others, like pacing back and forth for no reason, or acting in a way that people have described as bizarre or unusual?
No... not really. I don't pace around. Like I said, I mostly just sit in the garage or at my desk. Nobody has told me I'm doing anything bizarre.
Are there any other beliefs you hold that your wife or colleagues have strongly disagreed with or found difficult to believe, aside from your concerns about the datasets?
No. Not that I can think of. They don't... they don't really know what I'm doing anyway. So, no. Just the data.
Have you ever had any experiences where your thoughts felt like they were being broadcast out loud, or felt as though someone else was putting thoughts into your mind that were not your own?
No... I don't really know what you mean by that. They're just my thoughts. Nobody can hear them, and nobody is putting them there.
Over the past six months, have you felt that your ability to experience pleasure or interest in your life has significantly diminished compared to how you felt before these problems at work began?

I suppose... yeah. I don't really do much lately. I can just sit at my desk for hours... or out in the garage. The telescope is usually just sitting there, still covered up. I used to like that stuff... going to astronomy nights, hiking... even mentoring the younger analysts at work. But... I don't know. I just don't feel much pull to start anything right now. Or talk to anyone.

Looking back at the years before these problems at work started, did you ever feel like you were struggling with these same symptoms—like having less energy, feeling less motivated, or finding it hard to connect with people—even when you didn't have these worries about the datasets?
No... I don't think so. Things were fine before all this. I just... I went to work and did my job. It wasn't like this back then.
